To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the first aspartic acid of the DQXD motif for human UDP-glucuronysyltransferase 10 interacts with UDP-glucuric acid during catalysis.
the first aspartic acid of the DQxDM motif for human UDP-glucuronoyltransferase 1a10 (UGT1A10) interacts with UDP-glucuric acid (UGlcUA) during catalysis.
the DQxD motif of UGT1As and UGT2Bs is critical for UDP-GlucUA binding and that the first aspartic acid of the DQxDM motif interacts with the glucuronide moiety of the cosubstrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of human UDP-glucuronyltransferases.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of UDP-glucuronidation by human UDP-glucurononsyltransferase (UGT).
the molecular mechanism of UDP-GlcNAc transferases (GTs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 393 DQMDNAK 399 region of human UDP-GlcUA-dependent glucuronosyltransferases interacts with the glucuronosyl moiety of UDP-glucuronyltransferase.
the D393 of the DQMDNAK motif of human UGTs is critical for the recognition and binding of the glucuronic moiety of UDP-glucuronyl transferase.

the first aspartate in DQxD motif is essential for UGT1A1 and UGT2A1 activity, whereas the first glutamine and the third residue are not essential for activity but can influence the substrate specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the first aspartic acid residue of the DQXD motif for human UDP-glucuronosytransferase 1a10 interacts with UDP-glucuronyl acid during catalysis.
the first aspartic acid of the DQxxD motif in UGTs is essential for the interaction with the glucuronyl moiety of UDP-glucuronyltransferase 1a10.
the DQxD motif is a critical determinant for UDP-Glc binding in UGTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the first aspartic acid of the DQXD motif in human UGT1As is important for the binding of the glucuronic group of the cosubstrate UDP-GlcUA.
the 393QMDNAK399 region of the C-terminal domain is critical for UDP-glucuronyltransferase activity of human UGT 1A10.
the DQxD motif is critical for the glucuronic binding site in UGTs.
